QF.id: IFSCA Introduction to AML CFT and PF_16

question.text: What is the primary role of the Financial Intelligence Unit - India (FIU-IND)?

answer.text: To receive, process, analyze, and disseminate information relating to suspected financial transactions
To directly investigate and prosecute money laundering offences in court
To grant banking licenses to financial institutions operating in India
To set monetary policy and regulate the foreign exchange market

explanation.text: The Logic: FIU-IND was established as the central national agency responsible for receiving, processing, analyzing, and disseminating information relating to suspect financial transactions. It acts as a central repository and intelligence hub, not as an investigating or prosecuting body. The Trap: Option B is tempting because FIU-IND coordinates closely with enforcement agencies, but it is not the direct investigating or prosecuting body — that role lies with the Enforcement Directorate and other law-enforcement agencies. FIU-IND's mandate is intelligence: receiving, analyzing and disseminating STRs, CTRs and other reports. Note: All IFSCA-regulated entities must register on the FINGate 2.0 Portal with FIU-IND — non-registration is treated as non-compliance with the IFSCA AML/CFT/KYC Guidelines.
